sections.name: intro_hook
sections.description: A deep drum and a bell strike at 0.000 s with the Piper's call; buzzing hurdy-gurdy drone, a wooden slit-drum heartbeat on the hook's 3+3+2, claves answer the pause.

sections.name: rats_awaken
sections.description: Stomps, claps, strumstick, shaker and plucky bass; tambourine; then kick, toms on the hook's tresillo and darbuka; the band answers the pause; ratchet + roll build into a one-eighth silence.

sections.name: first_drop
sections.description: The whole town dances: kick + big drum, galloping bass with sub, toms on 3+3+2, claps and rope snare, tambourine 16ths, cajon, darbuka, psaltery chops, buzzing hurdy-gurdy; a fiddle doubles the flute; every pause is answered by the band.

sections.name: betrayal
sections.description: The cadence turns: Bb (bII) then Eb (the tritone) under an A drone that will not move; half-time toms; a unison hit and a silence with only stomps; the Piper's giggle echoes; the groove re-ignites on E with a chromatic creep.

sections.name: piper_returns
sections.description: The hook returns darker and stranger: airy, shadowed flute with a ghost tenor 28 cents flat, a dark fiddle an octave below, A against Bb in drone and high psaltery, a clockwork psaltery ostinato begins; the giggle lands on Bb and its echo answers wrong.

sections.name: final_drop
sections.description: Strongest section: flute + fiddle unison + soprano octave (+ low fiddle in the second pass), kick + big drum, sub bass, toms, son-clave claves, woodblock clockwork, cajon, tambourine, psaltery ostinato and chops, buzzing hurdy-gurdy counter-line; the second pass loses its pause and ends in a stutter, then everything stops for the Piper.

sections.name: disappearance
sections.description: Layers vanish bar by bar while the pulse keeps walking; the flute is left alone with a high bowed A and a wooden heartbeat; its last giggle and G#4 pickup lead straight back into the opening (loop).

accents.description: Drum + bell + flute hook at 0.000 s (A4)
Tritone D#5 hang -- the Piper's signature note
Flute giggle E6 E6 B5, echoed by plucked psaltery
Kick, toms (3+3+2) and darbuka enter; low fiddle shadows the flute
First band answer in the hook's pause (strings + toms + wood + bass)
Ratchet + snare roll + tom fill into the drop
FIRST DROP downbeat (kick + big drum + timpani + bell)
Band answers the pause on 3+3+2 (strings, toms, wood, bass)
Soprano octave joins, ornamented hook, tresillo stomps, anvil
Band answers the pause on 3+3+2 (strings, toms, wood, bass)
Harmony betrays: Bb under the hook, gong
Half-time on the tritone Eb, low tenor recorder, fiddles swell
Unison hit, then the rhythmic pause (only stomps)
Silence except stomps; the giggle echoes a semitone flat
Groove re-ignites on E; chromatic creep E-F-F#-G-G# in flute and fiddles
The Piper returns (darker hook); clockwork ostinato starts
Giggle lands on Bb5 and bends down; its echo answers a semitone sharp
Kick/stomp 16ths, tom fill, ratchet, snare roll -> silence
Second pass: flute trills, low fiddle, doubled stomps/claps, woodblock clockwork, high bowed E6
No pause anymore: the call repeats where the giggle was
Obsessive stutter bar: 16th bass, band stabs on every beat
Bass gone; kick filtered; giggle echoed
Kick gone; stomps, claps and the wooden heartbeat
Stomps and slit drum only; a high bowed A hangs in the air
G#4 pickup resolves into the A4 + drum at 0.000 s (seamless loop)

shots.picture: Moonlit street: the procession of children walks in lockstep behind the Piper (heel strikes on the beats); every head snaps to camera on the D#5 hang
shots.music: drum + bell + flute call at 0.000; D#5 hang 1.32

shots.picture: Extreme close-up of the Piper playing; eyes open on the claves, fingers lift on the giggle notes (real fingering)
shots.music: pause; claves 1.99/2.10; giggle E6 E6 B5

shots.picture: Day, sepia (back in time): rats pour out of a drain grate on 32nd-note spacing across the street
Rats gallop along the roof ridges; grain sacks burst on the tambourine and rats spill under the stall
The merchant yanks the barrel lid on the downbeat; rats burst out on the toms (3+3+2); he recoils
The baker recoils (stab 1), a merchant leaps onto a table (stab 2), a cat arches and backs away from the swarm
The city gate grinds open on the ratchet; a backlit silhouette in the fog steps through in the silence
FIRST DROP: tracking shot as the Piper strides through the market; the crowd turns toward him in a wave on the beats
Heads snap to him on the two band stabs; he bows and tips his hat on the giggle
The council chamber (callback to the studio's council scene): he offers; the mayor nods on the beats; a rat runs over the table
He raises the recorder; the fingering follows the real cadence notes
shots.music: cadence F E C B C B G#

shots.picture: Rat's-eye view: scurrying rats freeze on the second note; ears twitch on each note; heads turn to camera on the hang
Rows of rats rise onto their hind legs on the two stabs and sway in time toward the Piper
Overhead: three counter-rotating rings of rats pulse on the kick around the walking Piper; the stream behind tightens into lockstep
Dusk on the Weser: the Piper on a rock, a river of rats flowing along the shore toward him
The rats leap into the water; ripples ring out; big rings on the half-time hits
Still water and his reflection; the last rings fade; small ripples on each stomp in the silence
The town bursts out: bunting rises on the beats; people jump up one per note of the chromatic creep
The whole town in the studio's squat-dance, in perfect sync; the Piper watches, utterly still
He holds out his hand; the mayor slams the chest of gold shut on the flute's falling Bb bend
Silent laughter shaking on the eighths; the councillor flicks him away on every beat
Close-up: his hand lowers, the smile disappears, the light drains from warm to cold
He walks away; his shadow climbs the wall; the sky time-lapses from day to night into the silence
FINAL DROP: the Piper alone in the moonlit street; shutters burst open and windows light up in an eighth-note cascade
Inside: a boy drops his wooden horse (stab 1), a girl turns (stab 2); the rat on the sill never moves
Doors open on the beats; children step out of the glowing doorways in matching strides
Children join the line one per eighth note; in the silence everyone freezes and turns to camera
Long tracking shot alongside the procession; lantern posts sweep past in the foreground; synchronised footsteps
Overhead: the procession snakes through the streets with long moon shadows
Six peaceful faces; one turns to camera on each tresillo accent
Silhouettes climb toward the mountain under a huge moon (the studio's silhouette style)
At the mountain passage the children vanish group by group on the stabs; the Piper steps in and it seals in the silence
A mother with a candle finds the empty bed
Abandoned toys on the floor at the open door; the horse still rocking
The empty street from the opening; a wooden toy on the cobbles; the legend card
The Piper's silhouette appears far down the street in the fog
He dissolves on the last giggle; the title; the frame settles on the opening composition (loop)

captions.text: THE TOWN WAS OVERRUN BY RATS.
A MYSTERIOUS STRANGER OFFERED A SOLUTION.
BUT THE TOWN REFUSED TO PAY.
THIS TIME, THE RATS STAYED STILL.
